item.title: Falcons have "no updates" on Week 2 quarterback situation
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Falcons are not ready to name a starting quarterback for Week 2.
item.content:encoded:
The Falcons are not ready to name a starting quarterback for Week 2.

Cooper Rush got bumped into the starting role after Tua Tagovailoa injured his oblique during practice last week and went 12-of-22 for 143 yards, a touchdown and two interceptions in a 20-13 loss to the Steelers. Undrafted rookie Jack Strand was the only other available quarterback because Michael Penix was inactive and head coach Kevin Stefanski said that he never considered putting Strand in against Pittsburgh.

On Monday, Stefanski said, via multiple reporters, that he had "no updates" on the health of Tagovailoa or Penix. Penix tore his ACL last season and was cleared for full football activities in late August. He also said that he has no timeline in mind to settle on a starter for Atlanta's home opener against the Panthers.

The Falcons will return to practice on Wednesday and the participation levels in that workout should give some idea of what direction things will go in Week 2.

item.title: ESPN, NFL Network now simulcast the same Monday night pregame show
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: For years, NFL fans who wanted to watch a Monday Night Football pregame show had their pick of two different options.
item.content:encoded:
For years, NFL fans who wanted to watch a Monday Night Football pregame show had their pick of two different options. Now? Not.

Monday Night Countdown, ESPN's longtime pregame show, is now shown on both ESPN and NFL Network, as a result of the deal that made ESPN the owner of NFL Media and the NFL a 10 percent owner of ESPN.

It's easy to see why ESPN and the NFL see this as a good thing, a cost-cutting move that means they're only producing one show instead of two.

For fans, however, fewer choices is a bad thing. Some fans preferred the NFL Network pregame show, which is now gone. And even for viewers who were watching Monday Night Countdown anyway, there are legitimate concerns that the stronger ties between ESPN and the NFL will mean even less independence in the coverage of the sport. More propaganda, less journalism.

Ultimately, the ESPN-NFL Media merger wasn't done for the fans. It was done for the bottom lines of ESPN and NFL Media, who can save money on production costs when putting one show on two channels.

item.title: Todd Monken says Deshaun Watson to start Week 2: "There were really good things on film"
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Despite Sunday's blowout loss, the Browns will continue to start Watson at quarterback.
item.content:encoded:
If you thought the Browns would stop playing Deshaun Watson after their Week 1 stinker — why?

Head coach Todd Monken said in his Monday video conference that Watson is set to start the team's Week 2 matchup with the Buccaneers in Tampa on Sunday.

Watson finished Sunday’s 34-10 loss 16-of-22 for 205 yards with one touchdown and one interception. Forty-six of those yards came on that TD pass to Denzel Boston, which came with 1:52 left in the fourth quarter.

“It’s only been two weeks that he’s gotten all the reps,” Monken said. “And there were some really good things on film — some things that you can build on. And there were some others that — you know, operationally, we’ve got to get better at. There’s concepts that, there’s only so many looks you get from week to week, be it red zone concepts, third-down concepts.

“I did think that when he had time, when he understood the concepts, he didn’t play tentative, that he let it rip. Even the touchdown at the end, sure that was garbage time, but that was on their [No.] 1 corner. That was one of their starters out there. And that was a communication between him and the receiver. So, there were a lot of things to build on. Was it perfect? Of course not, otherwise we wouldn’t have scored as few of points as we did. But I’d like to see how we can build on that. I like his week of practice last week. And I think he’s only going to continue to get better.”

Monken said there wasn’t much discussion about potentially replacing Watson as QB1 after his Sunday performance.

“No, just confirmed it when I looked at the tape,” Monken said. “We’ve got to play better around him. We’ve got to call it better. And he’s got to play better.

“Our inability to function consistently as an offense was a byproduct of we — coaching and playing.”

While Watson threw an interception to end Cleveland’s first drive, Monken said he didn’t feel like the quarterback got tentative when it came to throwing downfield after that play.

“I would say that some of those weren’t called,” Monken said. “[T]here were times where we were trying to push the ball down the field and he did have a missed throw once we moved the pocket one time. But I know right before halftime, he made two great throws that put us in position. And then we got a couple of holding calls that had nothing to do with Deshaun.

“So, without watching the tape, you could say that — you could say, hey, he looked a little tentative there. And it’d be like, no, not really. Really, we just didn’t call certain routes to push it down the field, or we didn’t execute.”

The real issue, according to Monken, is that the club had “too many Browns hurting Browns moments.”

“And then even as we got later in the game, I did not see that one bit — that he was tentative in terms of trying to throw it down the field,” Monken said. “Sure, there’s a couple of times maybe he could’ve pumped it down there. But in my mind, I didn’t see that.”

Maybe we’ll all see something different in Week 2 when Cleveland plays Tampa Bay.

item.title: Seahawks say Sam Darnold's "very unique" injury has "no firm timeline"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Seattle offers more transparency than the injury report requires.
item.content:encoded:
The silver lining in the dark cloud of a quarterback injury is the potential strategic advantage it can create.

And the Seahawks seem to be leaning fully into the potential uncertainty flowing from Sam Darnold's Week 1 mishap, which reportedly caused a strained glute tendon.

Via Andrew Destin of The Athletic, a Seahawks spokesperson said Monday that Darnold has a "very unique, soft-tissue injury.” The Seahawks call it "short term," but they also acknowledged there is “no firm timeline.”

On Sunday, we reported that Darnold could be out four to six weeks.

The Seahawks have no obligation to say anything about Darnold, beyond the rules of the injury report. And that's a basic, bare-bones mandate — whether and to what extent he practiced on three days before a given game (limited or full) and, in the final report, whether he's questionable, doubtful, or out.

Teams love to force opposing defenses to prepare for multiple quarterbacks. If Darnold does enough on Wednesday, Thursday, and/or Friday to be described as participating in practice on a "limited" basis, they can keep the Cardinals guessing as to whether it will be Darnold or Drew Lock on Sunday.

And the Seahawks can keep doing that until Darnold returns.

Whatever the specific problem, it was sufficiently unique and confounding to result in up to four second opinions, as Jay Glazer of Fox Sports reported on Sunday. The thinking is they'll be cautious with Darnold, given that their team is good enough to win without him — and given the risk that he could suffer an aggravation that extends his absence.

item.title: DeMeco Ryans on Texans defense: I don't believe in hype, this isn't 2025, we have to earn it
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Leading up to the 2026 season, there was plenty of talk about how good the Texans defense could be — that the unit could help lead Houston to a deep postseason run.
item.content:encoded:
Leading up to the 2026 season, there was plenty of talk about how good the Texans defense could be — that the unit could help lead Houston to a deep postseason run.

But then Week 1 happened, with the Texans letting up 409 yards and 36 points in the loss to the Bills.

Buffalo does have one of the league’s best quarterbacks in Josh Allen and continuity on offense with former coordinator Joe Brady getting promoted to head coach. So the Bills have the potential to do that to many teams.

Still, it was a disappointing opening for a team that finished No. 1 in yards allowed and No. 2 in points allowed last year.

So did the Texans buy into the offseason hype too much? Did they consume the proverbial rat poison?

“I don't know,” head coach DeMeco Ryans said in his Monday press conference, via transcript from the team. “You have to ask those guys about the hype. I don't believe in hype. You've heard me stand here many times and talk about people talking about how great the defense was. Yeah, that was 2025. You don't just line up, and it's 2026, and just because you were good last year, you got to go out and make the plays. We made plays.

“The difference in this game on Sunday, versus the time we played the guys last year, we took the ball away three times. We go into this game, we don't take the ball away at all. We turn the ball over two times and we don't play smart defensively. We're not where we're supposed to be. We know the quarterback is going to scramble out to our left — if we don't stay out to our left and the quarterback runs for a touchdown, they're going to make plays.”

Ryans added that whatever Houston does this year, it’s not about how good the unit has been in the past.

“You have to put your stamp each and every year on who you're going to be,” Ryans said. “This is a new team. This isn't 2025. You have to go earn it. That's every year in the league, you have to go prove yourself. You can talk about it all you want to, how good you want to be, what are you going to do. You have to go out and make plays.

“That's always been my message. My message never changes. Talk never matters. When the ball is snapped, what are you doing?”

The Texans will be challenged defensively once again in Week 2, as the Bengals will be in town to face the club at 1 p.m. ET.

item.title: PFT's Week 2 2026 NFL power rankings
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The champs hang on, barely.
item.content:encoded:
1. Seahawks (last week No. 1; 1-0): They can win with Drew Lock. It's unknown how long they'll have to try to do that.

2. Bills (No. 5; 1-0): If winning a regular-season game got Joe Brady to take off his shirt, he'll be butt naked if they win in the playoffs.

3. Bears (No. 6; 1-0): The 59 offense is possibly better than the 46 defense.

4. Texans (No. 3; 0-1): Scoring 31 points should be more than enough for that defense.

5. Jaguars (No. 9; 1-0): They won 34-10, and it felt way more lopsided than that.

6. Ravens (No. 10; 1-0): Derrick Henry may never lose a step.

7. Bengals (No. 11; 1-0): In past years, they would have fully blown a 27-10 lead.

8. Chiefs (No. 13; 1-0): Kenneth Walker III earned every penny of his contract in his debut, and then some.

9. Eagles (No. 8; 1-0): A Week 1 escape vs. the Commanders answered no questions about whether they'll be true contenders.

10. 49ers (No. 15; 1-0): They turned the page decisively on all of those bizarre offseason storylines.

11. Rams (No. 2; 0-1): They're already all alone in last place of the NFC West.

12. Broncos (No. 4; 0-1): Maybe they should have tried to get Drew Brees to come back for last night's game, too.

13. Patriots (No. 7; 0-1): Fortunately, blowing it twice in the same game counts as only one loss.

14. Lions (No. 14; 1-0): The Lions had better hope the Saints are destined to be really good this year.

15. Vikings (No. 19; 1-0): For the second straight year, the Vikings woke up just in time to get a key division win in Week 1.

16. Giants (No. 20; 1-0): Jaxson Dart is the real deal, as long as he can stay healthy.

17. Steelers (No. 18; 1-0): For the second time in three years, T.J. Watt personally delivered a win over the Falcons in Week 1.

18. Cardinals (No. 32; 1-0): Jacoby Brissett is better than you realize.

19. Chargers (No. 12; 0-1): Who's got it better than us? Don't ask.

20. Packers (No. 16; 0-1): Matt LaFleur should be very happy he got that extension.

21. Saints (No. 24; 0-1): They may already be the best team in the division.

22. Cowboys (No. 17; 0-1): Like every year, the offseason's delusion gets a hard dose of reality.

23. Panthers (No. 21; 0-1): The Panthers have only themselves to blame for giving the Bears the pick that became Caleb Williams.

24. Buccaneers (No. 22; 0-1): The Browns are the perfect antidote to a Week 1 clunker.

25. Colts (No. 23; 0-1): They get plenty of hype every year, and they ultimately don't deliver.

26. Jets (No. 29; 1-0): Welcome back, Geno.

27. Raiders (No. 30; 1-0): They started 1-0 last year, too.

28. Commanders (No. 27; 0-1): At least they didn't get blown out.

29. Falcons (No. 25; 0-1): Maybe they should have just kept Kirk Cousins.

30. Titans (No. 26; 0-1): It could be another long year in Nashville.

31. Dolphins (No. 28; 0-1): They aren't tanking; they're just not good.

32. Browns (No. 31; 0-1): Prediction — Dillon Gabriel will be the starter by Week 10.

item.title: Sean McVay: We thought Myles Garrett's knee injury was something he could work through
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Before Sunday's games kicked off, there was big news involving a team that had opened its season earlier in the week.
item.content:encoded:
Before Sunday's games kicked off, there was big news involving a team that had opened its season earlier in the week.

Rams defensive end Myles Garrett needs knee surgery and will miss at least four games because he'll be placed on injured reserve while he recovers. The news came after Garrett made no impact in last Thursday's loss to the 49ers and cited his health — his practice time was limited all summer because of the knee — as a reason for his ineffectiveness.

On Monday, Rams head coach Sean McVay said, via multiple reporters, that the team thought the injury was ""something that he would be able to work through."

"Thought we would take an approach where he'd be feeling good enough to go contribute positive change and be the player that he's capable of," McVay said, via Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com. "That wasn't the case. And so the next right thing for us is to be able to get this thing fixed."

McVay said the team will not have a firm idea about Garrett's timeline to return to action until after the surgery. They know that it will be at least four games, however, and they know that their margin for error got a lot slimmer with or without him thanks to their dud in the opener.

item.title: Kenneth Walker runs for 60-yard TD on fourth down
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Chiefs needed 1 yard on a fourth-down play at their own 40.
item.content:encoded:
The Chiefs needed 1 yard on a fourth-down play at their own 40. They got 60.

Kansas City's prize offseason acquisition, Super Bowl LX MVP Kenneth Walker, got loose around the right side after Broncos cornerback Riley Moss missed the tackle. Safety Brandon Jones was the only defender who had a chance to stop Walker after that and appeared to have the angle.

He didn't.

Walker has 16 carries for 149 yards and a touchdown in his Chiefs' debut, the second-most yards of his career. He had 23 carries for 167 yards and two touchdowns in his sixth career game, which was against the Chargers.

Walker is 4-for-4 on third-and-1 or fourth-and-1 tonight.

The Chiefs lead 21-7.

item.title: Bo Nix throws TD on Broncos' second drive to forge a tie
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Bo Nix didn't get his season off to the best start, throwing an interception that set up the Chiefs at the Denver 46.
item.content:encoded:
Bo Nix didn't get his season off to the best start, throwing an interception that set up the Chiefs at the Denver 46. The Broncos quarterback responded on the next drive, though.

He completed passes of 13, 4, 8, 11 and 19 yards on his five passes on the second possession. The 19-yarder was a touchdown throw to Evan Engram.

It tied the game 7-7.

Nix is now 5-of-6 for 55 yards with a touchdown and an interception.

Wide receiver Pat Bryant has three catches for 32 yards.

item.title: With 42 points in Broncos-Chiefs, the Week 1 scoring record will be broken
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Through 15 games, 750 points have been scored.
item.content:encoded:
Led by the Bears' 59-point explosion in Charlotte, the NFL's first week of the season has seen pinball machine-level scoring.

And the all-time Week 1 record is in reach.

Via Mark Maske of Front Office Sports, the 750 total points scored through 15 games fall only 41 short of the all-time Week 1 record. So with 42 or more between the Broncos and Chiefs on Monday night, the record will fall.

In his first Week 1 without coaching one of the NFL's 32 teams since 2006 (when he was the Vikings' defensive coordinator), Mike Tomlin shared his thoughts on the matter on NBC. He pointed to the current methods of practice and preparation.

"There's less violence in team development," Tomlin said. "There are less padded practices. And even the drills that they do are more geared toward skill development, 7-on-7, and things of that nature. Defenses spend less time shedding blocks and tackling than they used to 25 years ago when I came in the league."

Tomlin has also said that mobile quarterbacks have an edge early in the year, because defenders aren't allowed to tackle quarterbacks in practice.

The NFL likes high-scoring games. Over the years, the rules have been tweaked to encourage more of it. Which means that there surely will be a press release on Tuesday with all sorts of statistics about the scoring in the Week 1 games.

And, with at least 42 points tonight, a headline that Week 1 of the 2026 season was the highest-scoring Week 1 of all time.

item.title: Drew Brees couldn't have unretired to play for Broncos in AFC Championship
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Brees remains on the Saints' reserve-retired list, and he couldn't have returned that last in the season.
item.content:encoded:
Sometimes, facts get in the way of a good story.

On Monday night, Adam Schefter of ESPN reported that quarterback Drew Brees considered emerging from retirement to play for the Broncos in the AFC Championship, given the injury that happened to starter Bo Nix late in the divisional-round win over the Bills.

There's only one problem with that. Brees, as PFT has confirmed, remains on the Saints' reserve-retired list. A retired player must return by the Tuesday after Week 13 in any given year. After that, he can't play for anyone.

Then there's the fact that the Saints would have had to release Brees from the reserve-retired list. He then would have been subject to waivers.

That doesn't mean the Broncos didn't talk to Brees, as Schefter reports. If, however, then-offensive coordinator Joe Lombardi and offensive assistant Pete Carmichael spoke to Brees without permission from the Saints, it would have been tampering.

Which leads to the next question. Will the league investigate the Broncos for tampering, based on Schefter's report? Even without a complaint from the Saints, the league could take action.

It never got to the point at which the Broncos or Brees realized that the rules would block the move, because Brees had "discomfort" in his wrist. Then there's the fact that Brees has said he can’t throw at all with his right arm due to his shoulder injury from 2005 — and that he throws better with his left.

So while the whole thing sounds good, it's a big, fat nothing burger which, if anything, will get the Broncos in hot water for tampering with a player whose rights remain with another team.

item.title: Monday Night Football: Kenneth Walker, Chiefs run by Broncos 31-10 in Patrick Mahomes' return
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Walker, who had a career-high 173 rushing yards, had more totals (191) than the Broncos had as a team (176).
item.content:encoded:
Kenneth Walker shared carries with Zach Charbonnet in Seattle. He is the man in Kansas City.

With Patrick Mahomes returning nine months after tearing his ACL and LCL, the Chiefs leaned on Walker and their run game in a 31-10 shellacking of the Broncos. The Chiefs threw 27 passes for 184 yards and ran 38 times for 220 yards.

It was the third-most rushing yards for an Andy Reid team in Kansas City.

Walker, the Super Bowl LX MVP who signed with the Chiefs in free agency, ran for 173 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries and caught three passes for 18 yards and a touchdown. It was the most rushing yards in his career, topping the 167 he had in his sixth career game.

Walker had more yards from scrimmage (191) than the Broncos had as a team (176).

Mahomes ran for a 15-yard touchdown and threw a 13-yard touchdown pass to Rashee Rice and a 2-yard touchdown pass to Walker, but he was only 15-of-27 for 184 yards and threw an interception.

Bo Nix had a terrible, horrible, no good, very bad day in his first game with Davis Webb as his playcaller and in his return from a season-ending ankle injury. The Broncos quarterback threw an interception and lost a fumble — and nearly lost another — while completing 17 of 28 passes for 131 yards with a touchdown and an interception.

His touchdown went 19 yards to Evan Engram, who led the Broncos with four catches for 43 yards.

The Broncos, who trailed only 14-7 at halftime, had only 15 carries for 61 yards.

item.title: Travis Kelce now second all-time in receiving yards for a TE
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce's longest reception last season was 44 yards.
item.content:encoded:
Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce's longest reception last season was 44 yards. His second catch of 2026 went 59 yards.

It was his longest reception since 2021, when he had a 69-yard catch against the Chargers in a Thursday night game.

On the catch, Kelce passed Jason Witten for second all-time in receiving yards by a tight end with 13,067. Tony Gonzalez holds the record with 15,127.

Kelce got the Chiefs to the 4, with Jahdae Barron saving the touchdown. They had to settle for Harrison Butker's chip-shot, 28-yard field goal.

The Chiefs lead 24-10.

item.title: Sean Payton: Broncos' loss starts with me, starts with our coaching staff
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Payton handed off play calling to offensive coordinator Davis Webb for the Broncos' 31-10 loss to the Chiefs.
item.content:encoded:
Broncos head coach Sean Payton was not happy with anyone on the team, least of all himself, after Monday night's 31-10 loss to the Chiefs.

"Obviously not a great evening. Didn't do a lot well at all in the game," Payton said. "That starts with me, that starts with our coaching staff. I thought they won, really, in every phase."

Payton handed over play calling to offensive coordinator Davis Webb, and Payton was asked afterward whether it was especially frustrating not to be in control of the offense.

"As a head coach, always, whether you're calling the plays or not — regardless of who's calling the plays, when you have a game like that and you're the head coach, it's frustrating, it's disappointing. I don't know that the feeling is any different whether you're calling them or not, honestly," Payton said.

The Broncos' two running backs, J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey, combined for just 11 carries for 54 yards. Payton said he would have liked to see more running the ball, but he wasn't necessarily blaming Webb for that. Payton noted that the Broncos consistently found themselves in long-yardage passing situations and were trailing for the entire second half.

"Our third down numbers weren't good, our rushing numbers weren't good, pick your spot," Payton said. "Lot of long yardage, lot of throws, not enough runs."

Asked how he'll evaluate Webb as a play caller going forward, Payton said he'll review his performance the way he would a player's.

"No different than a player, just evaluating the first quarter, the game, and then making the corrections and learning," Payton said.

The Broncos have a lot of corrections to make.

item.title: Patrick Mahomes: Rushing TD gave me confidence I could be myself
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Mahomes also threw two TDs in his return from a torn ACL.
item.content:encoded:
One of Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes's greatest gifts on the football field has been his ability to make plays with his feet when things break down and whether he'd be able to do that after last season's torn ACL was one of the biggest questions around his return to action on Monday night.

It didn't take long for Mahomes to show that he still has that part of his game. On the 10th play of Kansas City's opening drive, Mahomes took off for a five-yard touchdown run only to see the play get called back for a holding penalty. Mahomes repeated the feat from 15 yards out on the next play and the Chiefs were on their way to a resounding 31-10 win over the Broncos.

In his postgame press conference, Mahomes said that "gave me that confidence that I can go out there and be myself."

“Physically, I think that’s the moment," Mahomes said. "I want to get some of these passes down the field a little bit more — I think that’ll help me out mentally and kinda get back in the rhythm of things. That was definitely the moment, physically, to say all this work has paid off. I didn't feel anything. It’s still a process, I got to still keep getting better and better, but this is obviously a great first week."

Mahomes ran seven times for 23 yards overall and was 15-of-27 for 184 yards, two touchdowns and an interception through the air. Those numbers don't jump off the page the way some of his past performances do, but context matters and the context of Monday night made it everything that the Chiefs could have hoped to see from their quarterback.

item.title: Kenneth Walker: Means a lot that the Chiefs trust me
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Kenneth Walker played his first game with the Chiefs on Monday night and head coach Andy Reid made it clear right off the bat that the free agent addition is going to be playing a major role in the offense.
item.content:encoded:
Kenneth Walker played his first game with the Chiefs on Monday night and head coach Andy Reid made it clear right off the bat that the free agent addition is going to be playing a major role in the offense.

After rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane intercepted Broncos quarterback Bo Nix to end Denver's first possession, Reid called four straight runs with Walker. The fourth of them was a fourth down conversion and Walker would get three more carries on the opening drive before Patrick Mahomes ended it with a touchdown run.

That set the Chiefs on their way to a 31-10 win and Walker would end the night with 26 total touches.

"It means a lot," Walker said. "It means they trust me. It’s good to feel that way."

Walker's touches resulted in 191 yards and two touchdowns, including a 60-yard lightning bolt on another fourth down early in the third quarter. Reid called that run "a thing of beauty" on a memorable night for the new Chief.

"You never know, going in, how many times you're going to give him the ball," Reid said. "That’s not a calculated thing, you gotta be making yards. For him to play the way he did, I thought it was spectacular. It was something you hope for, and you got to see it, where he was the main guy. Did a great job with it.”

Walker's final game with the Seahawks was Super Bowl LX and he was named the MVP of that victory. His first game with the Chiefs carried a little less weight, but he left just as strong an impression on those who were watching him in action.

item.title: Chiefs CB Mansoor Delane to have MRI on shoulder
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Chiefs first-round pick Mansoor Delane had a brief, but eventful NFL debut on Monday night.
item.content:encoded:
Chiefs first-round pick Mansoor Delane had a brief, but eventful NFL debut on Monday night.

Delane recorded his first interception as a pro when he snagged a pass from Broncos quarterback Bo Nix on the third play of the game. That would be the last contribution of the night for the rookie cornerback, however.

Delane went to the locker room with a shoulder injury during the Broncos' second offensive possession. Head coach Andy Reid did not have an update on his condition after the game and Mike Garafolo of NFL Media reports that he will have an MRI on Tuesday.

Garafolo adds that X-rays were negative and that there is hope that Delane, who also dealt with a shoulder injury in the spring, emerged with a sprain. Tuesday's test should provide a better picture of how long it will be before he's back in the Kansas City secondary.

item.title: Mike LaFleur: Confidence is great, but we have to reset and get back to work
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Cardinals pulled off the biggest upset of Week 1, but Monday wasn't a day for reveling in their 26-14 win over the Chargers.
item.content:encoded:
The Cardinals pulled off the biggest upset of Week 1, but Monday wasn't a day for reveling in their 26-14 win over the Chargers.

Head coach Mike LaFleur's message was about the next game on the schedule rather than on rehashing all that went right in his Arizona debut. The Cardinals will face the Seahawks in Week 2 and the coach said that he is drilling down on the message that the Cardinals have to start back from square one as they prepare to host the defending champs.

"Confidence is great, but like I told them today, 'We got to reset and get right back to work,'" LaFleur said, via the team's website. "This is a week-to-week league, and your goal is to go 1-0 every weekend. We're not going to talk anything past that. Obviously we got the result, but we're right back to work."

LaFleur's directive met a willing recipient in wide receiver Kendrick Bourne. He acknowledged that "building from success is better" than the alternative, but added that the team has to hone "little details" in order to be more than a one-week wonder.

item.title: Sunday Ticket prices increase, while NFL decreases the number of Sunday afternoon games
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: A quarter-century ago, NFL Sunday Ticket felt like a modern miracle to football fans.
item.content:encoded:
A quarter-century ago, NFL Sunday Ticket felt like a modern miracle to football fans. What once was an impossible dream, being able to watch any NFL game you wanted on Sunday afternoon, was now a reality. Fans who could previously only watch a game or two on Sunday could now have their pick of more than a dozen. It was an astonishing luxury to have all those games just a remote click away.

Sunday Ticket is still a popular item for football fans, but it has lost some luster. There are now so many opportunities to watch the NFL, on so many days of the week, that it's much easier for fans to feel like they're getting their fill by watching only the games that air on prime time or on their local affiliates on Sunday afternoon, without needing Sunday Ticket.

In 2002, the first season when the NFL had 32 teams, there were 17 Monday night games, 16 Sunday night games, three Thursday games and five Saturday games. Everything else was on Sunday afternoon.

In 2025, there were 21 Monday night games, 18 Sunday night games, six Sunday morning international games, 21 Thursday games (including three on Christmas Day), six Saturday games and two Friday games. Far fewer games were on Sunday afternoon.

So for the 2002 season, 215 of the NFL's 256 games (84 percent) were on Sunday afternoon. By 2025, when the season was one week longer, only 198 of 272 games (73 percent) were on Sunday afternoon.

Many Sunday Ticket subscribers get the service because they want to watch their favorite team, but don't live in their favorite team's market. But Sunday Ticket is increasingly unnecessary for fans of popular teams that are frequently shown on national television. Last year the Chiefs and Cowboys each played eight games that were either on Sunday night or another day of the week, and many of their Sunday afternoon games were shown across most of the country by Fox or CBS. If you're a Chiefs fan outside Kansas City or a Cowboys fan outside Dallas, it's a rare week when you need Sunday Ticket to watch your team.

And missing a game just isn't as big a deal today as it was in the early days of Sunday Ticket because there are so many opportunities to see what you're missing: If you have RedZone channel, you'll see all the big plays from every game, and even if you don't have RedZone, highlights are all over social media.

As the necessity of Sunday Ticket decreases, its prices increase: In 2023, YouTube took Sunday Ticket over from DirecTV, which had it from its inception. According to the Wall Street Journal, YouTube has increased the price of Sunday Ticket by almost 30 percent while the number of games available has declined.

The biggest NFL fans, the ones who love nothing more than spending a Sunday afternoon watching multiple games on multiple screens, will keep paying. But for a lot of fans, more money for fewer games is increasingly looking like a bad deal.

item.title: Matt LaFleur saw "protection busts that should not and cannot happen" on Vikings film
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Packers quarterback Jordan Love was pressured relentlessly by the Vikings' defense in Sunday's 39-22 loss, and Matt LaFleur said after watching the film that the pass protection needed to be a lot better.
item.content:encoded:
Packers quarterback Jordan Love was pressured relentlessly by the Vikings' defense in Sunday's 39-22 loss, and Matt LaFleur said after watching the film that the pass protection needed to be a lot better.

"I saw some of the things we have to clean up," LaFleur said. "What’s disappointing is, we had a few protection busts that should not and cannot happen. We knew that was the challenge going in. They were gonna give some tough looks. That’s the toughest test you’re going to face Week 1, to play that defense in that environment. I thought there was some really good stuff, but when your quarterback gets hit 15 times, that's too many times. There are some things we could do schematically that we've got to do a better job with and there are some things we have to go out and execute. But we have to have everybody on the same page if we want to give ourselves a chance."

LaFleur also noted that the Packers' passing game had several explosive plays when they took advantage of the Vikings' blitzing. Love finished with 387 passing yards and an impressive average of 18.4 yards per completion, but ultimately the Vikings' defense got to Love too often.

"We had some great moments when we feasted on it, certainly, but at the end of the game when we needed to make plays, they did what they do," LaFleur said.

What the Vikings do under defensive coordinator Brian Flores is relentlessly pressure the quarterback, and that happened a lot on Sunday.

item.title: Monday Night Football: Chiefs lead the Broncos 14-7 at halftime
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Patrick Mahomes isn't completely back from his knee injury, but he has accounted for two touchdowns and the Chiefs lead the Broncos 14-7 at halftime.
item.content:encoded:
Patrick Mahomes isn't completely back from his knee injury, but he has accounted for two touchdowns and the Chiefs lead the Broncos 14-7 at halftime.

Mahomes ran for a 15-yard touchdown on the Chiefs' first series. The 10-play, 46-yard drive was set up by rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane's interception of Bo Nix on the third play.

The Chiefs had only 15 plays for 39 yards on their next three possessions before going 80 yards in 10 plays. Rashee Rice had a 13-yard catch-and-run for a touchdown on a pass from Mahomes.

Mahomes is only 8-of-18 for 62 yards and a touchdown after starting 2-for-12. He has completed a pass to six different wide receivers.

He also has two rushes for 23 yards and a touchdown.

Mahomes was a long shot to play the season opener after tearing the ACL and LCL in his left knee on Dec. 14. He underwent reconstructive surgery the following day.

The Chiefs, though, have leaned on their running game and their Super Bowl MVP running back. Kenneth Walker has 14 carries for 89 yards, tying the most rushes in the first half of a game started by Mahomes, and also has two catches for 16 yards.

The Chiefs have outgained the Broncos 182 to 113.

Nix is 12-of-17 for 98 yards with a touchdown and an interception, with Pat Bryant catching four passes for 42 yards. Evan Engram scored on a 19-yard reception.

The Broncos have only six rushes for 23 yards.

item.title: NAACP president Derrick Johnson will appear on ESPN to discuss Protect College Sports Act
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: After ESPN gave Senator Ted Cruz (R-Texas) a platform to push for the Protect College Sports Act, with no opposing view offered, the NAACP challenged ESPN to provide its president, Derrick Johnson, with a similar opportunity this weekend, when College GameDay goes to Oxford, Mississippi.
item.content:encoded:
After ESPN gave Senator Ted Cruz (R-Texas) a platform to push for the Protect College Sports Act, with no opposing view offered, the NAACP challenged ESPN to provide its president, Derrick Johnson, with a similar opportunity this weekend, when College GameDay goes to Oxford, Mississippi.

Johnson will appear on ESPN, but not on Saturday.

Via John Ourand of Puck, ESPN has booked Johnson to appear on Tuesday's SportsCenter at 6:00 p.m. ET.

ESPN offered airtime on Tuesday, in the event the Senate votes on the bill before Saturday. Regardless, it will be a much smaller audience than the GameDay viewership.

And even if the Senate votes by Saturday, the bill will still go to the House of Representatives. The only way to truly balance Saturday's gesture would be to give someone from the opposing side the same runway Cruz received on Saturday.

At this point, of course, it's more about P.R. and less about truly presenting the opposing view. Based on Disney's lobbying efforts, the company wants the bill to pass.

item.title: Landon Dickerson: I was a complete liability; I should not be out there until healthy
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Eagles will place left guard Landon Dickerson on injured reserve with a knee injury.
item.content:encoded:
The Eagles will place left guard Landon Dickerson on injured reserve with a knee injury.

Dickerson appeared on WIP's "Players Lounge Show" as news hit that he was headed to IR with what he described as a bone bruise in his right knee.

He said he "played like shit" in the Eagles' 24-22 win over the Commanders on Sunday.

“I was a complete liability yesterday," Dickerson said, via Alexis Chassen of bleedinggreennation.com. "Again, that was my fault. I know I said earlier in camp I shouldn’t be out there until I feel healthy. A few weeks ago, [I] got rolled up on in practice. I thought as weeks went by it would get better. It didn’t, and we kind of went out there and finally got some imaging on it today, figured out what was wrong with it.

"Really the best plan going forward is to put me on IR, so I can get this thing better to have a good stretch at the back end of the season versus kind of what happened last year, go out there limping through 18 weeks. I don’t think anyone wants to see that again because that was just ugly. I don’t want to do that again, because that was just some BS.”

Dickerson underwent surgery in August 2025 to repair an injured meniscus and appeared in 15 games, though he later admitted he could have used more rehab time. He went to Columbia for stem cell therapy this offseason.

Drew Kendall, a fifth-round pick in 2025, could replace Dickerson.

item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Eagles guard Landon Dickerson will miss at least the next four weeks.
item.content:encoded:
Eagles guard Landon Dickerson will miss at least the next four weeks.

Dickerson is going on injured reserve, according to Jeff McLane of the Philadelphia Inquirer.

In Sunday's opener against the Commanders, Dickerson had a rough day in pass protection, although Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni praised his run blocking. Although the exact nature of Dickerson's injury has not been reported, it appears Dickerson was playing through something, and he and the team have now decided he needs at least a month to get healthy.

Dickerson said this offseason that he has rethought his approach to playing through injuries, although he denied talk that he was thinking about retiring because of the physical toll that football has taken on his body.

The 27-year-old Dickerson was a second-round pick of the Eagles in 2021 and is a three-time Pro Bowler.

The Eagles will likely go with either Drew Kendall or Willie Lampkin at left guard while Dickerson is out.

item.title: Mike McCarthy noncommittal on Joey Porter's return timeline
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. didn't play in Sunday's season-opening win over the Falcons, and coach Mike McCarthy was noncommittal on Porter's timeline for a return.
item.content:encoded:
Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. didn't play in Sunday's season-opening win over the Falcons, and coach Mike McCarthy was noncommittal on Porter's timeline for a return.

Porter, who did not get his desired contract extension with the team before the start of the season, missed all of training camp with a back injury. He was limited in practice last week, and McCarthy said Porter was in a "ramp-up" period.

McCarthy was asked Monday whether the plan was to increase Porter's workload this week.

"Hopefully we’ll have a good plan for him on Wednesday, and hopefully we'll do more," McCarthy said, via Brooke Pryor of ESPN. "That's the outlook. So yeah, hopefully we move forward with more volume of work. That would be my anticipation."

McCarthy did add that he expects Porter to play once the ramp-up is completed.

Porter has not publicly committed to playing.

He is due to make $3.924 million in 2026 and wants a deal commensurate with those of Devon Witherspoon and Christian Gonzalez. The Steelers stop negotiations once the season starts, so a trade is a possibility with Porter in the final year of his deal.

Pryor reports the Steelers have neither made nor received calls for the 2023 second-round pick.

"My concern for Joey, obviously, is to get him to a spot no different than everybody else in training camp," McCarthy said. "The first players that go through that first ramp-up period that are not ready to go -- they don't participate fully in a padded practice. So I don't really see this any different than that. Now it is different that there's a business component to it, and that's really a whole other topic.

"As far as Joey's participation in practice, he's communicating with the trainer every day. He's communicating with the strength and conditioning coach. . . . We'll get him out there when he's ready to go through a full practice."

item.title: Quinnen Williams: We really need to be critical to get better
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: One of the focal points for the Cowboys this offseason was getting better on defense, but their first outing of the year didn't show the kind of improvement they were looking for in Dallas.
item.content:encoded:
One of the focal points for the Cowboys this offseason was getting better on defense, but their first outing of the year didn't show the kind of improvement they were looking for in Dallas.

The Giants put up 394 yards and drove for four touchdowns over the course of Sunday night's 28-20 win. They converted nine of their 11 third down opportunities, which gave them possession of the ball for nearly 37 minutes and was the thing defensive tackle Quinnen Williams identified as the biggest problem with the unit's effort.

"I think we definitely gotta be critical [of ourselves] in our approach, when we get to [preparing for Week 2]. And it's a great week to learn, and to get things better," Williams said, via the team's website. "The guys we got in our locker room, especially on defense, are unbelievable when it comes down to taking constructive criticism and accountability, first of all, and let's move," he said. "We had a lot of mental errors, a lot of busts today, and just really need to be critical with that going into this week; and focus on getting better."

A Week 1 loss doesn't close many doors — the Patriots and Seahawks were both 0-1 last season — but teams can't be shy about addressing what didn't work as they move toward future games. The Cowboys will put that to the test as they get ready for the Commanders in Week 2.

item.title: Marshall Faulk acknowledges the reality of early-season "crash-test dummy" games
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The new age of college football has made one of its time-honored traditions even more glaring — the early-season tuneup games.
item.content:encoded:
The new age of college football has made one of its time-honored traditions even more glaring — the early-season tuneup games.

First-year Southern coach Marshall Faulk witnessed it on Saturday, when No. 22-ranked Houston shredded his Jaguars, 77-6.

"That wasn't really a game, that was kind of a preseason crash-dummy test for Houston to work on all the good plays," Faulk told reporters, via Brad Crawford of CBS Sports.

Southern was paid $450,000 to serve as the cannon fodder for the Cougars.

For decades, high-level programs have scheduled lower-level schools in the early weeks of the season. What used to be games between Division I-A and Division I-AA have become FBS vs. FCS slaughterhouses.

"Let's just be real, OK?" Faulk said. "They're better than us. We're FCS, everybody knows what this is, let it be what it is."

The transfer portal has made matters worse, because the best young players at FCS schools typically end up getting big bucks with FBS programs.

"I was literally standing on the sideline thinking to myself, back when let's say Southern had juniors and seniors . . . this could be a competitive game playing a team like Houston," Faulk said. "In today's landscape, we don't have the budget to compete against them. We just don't."

Saturday's game included an eight-minute fourth quarter, after Houston built a 70-0 lead through the first 45 minutes.

"The reality is our kids were giving their best effort, but we're not good enough to beat a team that doesn't beat themselves," Faulk said. "There's not anything we could've done. I've been around a lot of football, man. We don't have the bodies, we don't have the funds, we don't have the equipment . . . all the stuff needed to compete with a team like that. . . . Guts and glory and want and will is not enough to compete with a team like that."

Again, it's been that way for a long time. Recent trends have made it worse. The question becomes whether the powers-that-be will change the rules to prevent games like this from happening.

The problem is that, even if the players have no business going against elite programs, their schools won't want to give up the revenue that comes from serving as a sacrificial lamb.
